holidays.name: National Pralines Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the sweet, creamy, nutty confection that Southern kitchens have turned into an art form. Grab a pecan praline and let it melt on your tongue.
holidays.origin: The praline was created in France in the 17th century, reportedly by the chef of Marshal du Plessis-Praslin, who coated almonds in caramelized sugar. French settlers brought the idea to New Orleans, where pecans replaced almonds and cream was added, creating the creamy version Americans love today.
holidays.funFact: The confection is named after the marshal's surname, Praslin, and the French and American versions are very different: French pralines are crunchy caramelized nuts, while New Orleans pralines are soft and fudgy.

holidays.name: International Fairy Day
holidays.description: A magical day for believing in fairies, pixies, and all things tiny and winged. People are encouraged to leave out small treats, build miniature fairy gardens, and keep an eye out for glimmers in the garden.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance falls near Midsummer, a time that folklore across Europe associates with fairies being most active and the veil between worlds growing thin. Midsummer's Eve traditions in Ireland, England, and Scandinavia include leaving offerings for the Fair Folk.
holidays.funFact: In Irish folklore, it was once considered wise to avoid certain hawthorn trees on Midsummer, because disturbing a fairy tree could bring terrible luck.

holidays.name: Take Your Dog to Work Day (Observed Around This Date)
holidays.description: A celebration of canine coworkers everywhere, when pups trade the couch for the cubicle. Expect extra morale, a few squeaky toys, and at least one meeting derailed by a Labrador.
holidays.origin: Pet Sitters International launched Take Your Dog to Work Day in 1996 to encourage people to adopt dogs from shelters by showing how well they fit into daily life. It is observed on the Friday after Father's Day in the United States, which often lands close to June 24.
holidays.funFact: The very first celebration reportedly had only a few hundred participating workplaces, but it has since grown to include millions of employees and their furry colleagues.

holidays.name: Celebration of the Senses Day
holidays.description: A day to pause, put down your phone, and fully experience the world through sight, sound, smell, taste, and touch. Bake bread and savor the aroma, listen to rain, or walk barefoot on grass.
holidays.origin: This is a mindfulness-style observance that encourages people to slow down and engage with everyday sensory pleasures. It grew out of the wellness and awareness movements that promote being present in the moment.
holidays.funFact: The human nose can distinguish at least one trillion different scents according to a widely cited 2014 study, though some scientists dispute the exact number.

holidays.name: Inti Raymi (Festival of the Sun)
holidays.description: A dazzling Incan winter solstice festival honoring the sun god Inti, with elaborate costumes, music, dancing, and ceremonial processions through Cusco, Peru.
holidays.origin: Inti Raymi was celebrated by the Inca Empire to thank the sun for the harvest and to ask for its return during the Southern Hemisphere's shortest days. Spanish colonizers banned it in 1572, but it was revived in 1944 as a theatrical reenactment.
holidays.funFact: The modern festival draws tens of thousands of spectators to Sacsayhuamán, an ancient fortress on a hill above Cusco, and the main performance is delivered largely in Quechua.
